key_insight: Fault-tolerant quantum compilers must become code-aware, hardware-aware, and decoder-aware so they can translate algorithms into reliable logical operations under QEC constraints.
engineering_relevance: This survey frames compiler design as a full-stack systems problem that directly affects whether practical fault-tolerant quantum computers can execute scalable workloads on real hardware.
method: Organizes FTQC compilation into three layers: logical-level QEC compilation, physical-level QEC realization, and decoder runtime integration.
Reviews surface-code lattice surgery, beyond-surface-code and qLDPC code-surgery ideas, plus non-Clifford support via magic-state distillation and code switching.
Covers hardware-specific realization for superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom platforms, along with real-time decoding and frame management.
evidence_signal: The paper is a survey of existing work and synthesizes cross-layer compiler, hardware, and decoder designs rather than reporting new benchmark results in the abstract.
watch_item: A key implementation risk is that qLDPC compilation and compiler-decoder co-design remain immature, so end-to-end stacks may be difficult to integrate and benchmark consistently.
paper_title: Quantum Compiler Design for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
